records.label: 3 brothers

accumulation of intermediate filaments 7-10 nm in cardiac muscle cells
myofibrillar disintegration with Z band changes and rod-like bodies
glycogen accumulation in cardiac muscle cells
filament deposits, SR proliferation and glycogen overload in a few skeletal muscle fibers

quotes: Unusual histological and ultrastructural changes in cardiac muscle cells have been found in 3 brothers with progressive myocardial deficiency.
The electron microscope showed that this material consisted of sinuous filaments, 7-10 nm in diameter, similar to the intermediate filaments normally present in cardiac muscle cells.
Discrete SR proliferation, glycogen overload and filament deposits were observed in a few skeletal fibres.

records.label: Family with cytoplasmic body myopathy (3 successive generations)
records.onset: about 40 years in the two older patients; 18 years in the youngest

phenotypes.text: numerous cytoplasmic (spheroid) bodies within type I muscle fibers

quotes: Three patients, 72, 45 and 18 years old belonging to 3 successive generations presented with respiratory insufficiency.
The clinical onset was at about 40 years of age in the two older patients and at 18 years in the youngest one.

Serum enzymes of muscle origin were within normal range as well as leucocyte maltase activity. The muscle biopsy in all three patients showed numerous cytoplasmic (spheroid) bodies within type I muscle fibers.

records.label: Japanese kindred
records.sex: males affected more often than females (2:1)

phenotypes.text: normal or slightly elevated serum creatine kinase
myopathic EMG with slight neurogenic change
cytoplasmic bodies in skeletal muscle, predominantly type I fibers
dense central cores of myofilaments with radiating filaments on electron microscopy

quotes: An autosomal dominant progressive myopathy with diffuse cytoplasmic bodies (CBs) is described. In four successive generations, 12 patients suffered from weakness and atrophy of muscles in the distal extremities, neck, thorax and shoulder girdles.
The mean age at onset was 42 years old, and the patients became disabled after 5 to 10 years due to chronic respiratory failure.
Autopsy of 2 cases revealed numerous CBs in the skeletal muscles. Smooth and cardiac muscles were also affected. CBs were present predominantly in type I fibers in skeletal muscles.

records.label: Two siblings

phenotypes.text: cardiomyopathy preceding muscle weakness by several years
subsarcolemmal eosinophilic crescents in type I and type II fibres
subsarcolemmal deposits immunoreactive for desmin and ubiquitin
granular and filamentous aggregates arising from Z-bands

quotes: Two siblings developed cardiomyopathy several years before slowly progressive muscle weakness. Skeletal muscle biopsy specimens showed subsarcolemmal crescents of dark eosinophilic material in both type I and type II fibres.
Immunohistochemically the subsarcolemmal material stained positively for the intermediate filament protein desmin and for the heat shock protein ubiquitin but for no other cytoskeletal proteins.
Ultrastructurally the subsarcolemmal deposits consisted of aggregates of granular and filamentous material arising from Z-bands.

records.label: Large kinship with autosomal dominant distal myopathy with desmin storage

phenotypes.text: distal leg weakness causing gait disturbance

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

phenotypes.text: short duration polyphasic motor unit potentials
phenotypes.hpo_label: Abnormal single motor unit action potential

quotes: A large family is described with an autosomal dominant distal myopathy

The disease begins in early to middle adulthood with gait disturbance due to distal leg weakness, and progresses over 5-10 years to involve all extremities, as well as bulbar, respiratory, and facial muscles.
There is frequent cardiac involvement, manifest by arrhythmias, conduction blocks, and congestive failure, resulting in premature demise.

records.label: 28-year-old man

phenotypes.text: desmin-immunoreactive sarcoplasmic granular and filamentous aggregates in skeletal muscle, myocardium and intestinal smooth muscle
neurofilament-immunoreactive axonal spheroids in spinal cord and roots

quotes: The present study focuses on a 28-year-old man with generalized muscular atrophy, cardiomyopathy, and intestinal malabsorption and pseudo-obstruction.

Abundant sarcoplasmic granular and filamentous aggregates that were ultrastructurally continuous with Z lines or dense bodies and exhibited intense immunostaining for desmin were present throughout the skeletal musculature, myocardium, and smooth muscle of the intestine.
Moreover, neurofilament-immunoreactive axonal spheroids were identified in the spinal cord and roots.

quotes: We report here a human patient with severe generalized myopathy and aberrant intrasarcoplasmic accumulation of desmin intermediate filaments.
Muscle tissue from this patient lacks the wild-type desmin allele and has a desmin gene mutation encoding a 7-aa deletion within the coiled-coil segment of the protein.

The L345P desmin missense mutation occurs in a large, six generation Ashkenazi Jewish family.

records.label: Swedish family

phenotypes.text: granulofilamentous changes and myofibrillar disorganization on electron microscopy

quotes: Twenty-one members of a Swedish family suffering from myopathy and cardiomyopathy underwent neurological and cardiological investigations.
Twelve patients had myopathy.

Three men had arrhythmogenic right ventribular cardiomyopathy. Nonsustained ventribular tachycardia, atrial flutter, and dilatation of the ventricles mainly affecting the right ventricle were documented.

records.label: Large family with hereditary distal myopathy
records.segregation: disease locus linked to 2q33 between D2S2248 and D2S401
quotes: We are investigating the genetics of a large family with an autosomal dominant form of hereditary distal myopathy. This slowly progressive myopathy begins during early adulthood in the distal leg muscles, producing a gait disturbance.
Cardiomyopathy is also present in most affected family members, manifesting itself as conduction block or congestive heart failure.
Histologically, an accumulation of the protein, desmin, occurs in the subsarcolemmal spaces of myofibers.

records.label: Patient with IVS2-1G-A
quotes: A G to A transition at the highly conserved -1 nucleotide position of intron 2 affecting the splice acceptor site (IVS2-1G-->A) was found in an unrelated patient with a similar phenotype.

records.label: Three families with skeletal or cardioskeletal myopathy
quotes: We have studied three families with skeletal or cardioskeletal myopathy caused by small in-frame deletions in the desmin gene.
The newly identified in-frame deletions E359_S361del and N366del alter the heptad periodicity within a critical 2B coiled-coil segment.

quotes: We report here on two distantly related Dutch families with autosomal dominant inheritance of desmin-related myopathy affecting 15 family members.
A highly heterogeneous clinical picture is apparent, varying from isolated dilated cardiomyopathy to a more generalised skeletal myopathy and mild respiratory problems.
In both families we identified an identical novel pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation, S13F, in the 'head' domain of the desmin gene which cosegregates with the disease phenotype.

records.label: LGMD1D/1E family (previously linked to 6q23)

phenotypes.text: cytoplasmic inclusions in skeletal muscle containing desmin

quotes: Limb girdle muscular dystrophy 1D/1E (OMIM nomenclature LGMD1D, Human Gene Nomenclature Committee LGMD1E), a skeletal and cardiac myopathy, has previously been linked to chromosome 6q23.

Sequencing in this patient and family members identified the genetic basis of the previously reported 6q23 linked LGMD1D/1E to be due to an intron splice donor site mutation (IVS3+3A>G) of the desmin gene located on chromosome 2q35.

records.label: Swedish family with autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy and ARVC
records.segregation: Found by Sanger sequencing in 7 of the 10 family members previously classified as affected (17 family members tested)
quotes: Using exome sequencing we searched for the genetic cause of autosomal dominant myofibrillar myopathy with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) in a Swedish family. A heterozygous C-to-T transition, c.1255C>T, p.Pro419Ser in the desmin gene on chromosome 2q35, was identified.
Sanger sequencing of DNA from 17 family members confirmed the heterozygous c.1255C>T desmin mutation in seven out of ten family members that had been classified as affected in the previous study.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

phenotypes.text: cardiomyopathy with transformation of clinical phenotypes over time

quotes: This report describes the first case of desmin cardiomyopathy with early manifestation in adolescence and transformation of several clinical phenotypes over time, representing sufficient difficulties for the correct clinical diagnosis and treatment of the disease at an early stage.

records.label: Consanguineous LGMD2 family

phenotypes.text: progressive proximal muscle weakness of shoulder and pelvic girdles
absence of myofibrillar disorganization and myofibrillar degradation products on ultrastructure

records.segregation: homozygous in the two affected family members; region identified by homozygosity mapping
quotes: Here we have investigated a consanguineous family with LGMD2 with two affected individuals in order to identify the causative gene defect.
DNA sequence analysis of the highly relevant candidate gene DES revealed a homozygous splice site mutation c.1289-2A>G in the two affected family members.

Unlike autosomal dominant desminopathies, ultrastructural alterations such as disruption of myofibrillar organisation, formation of myofibrillar degradation products and dislocation/aggregation of membranous organelles were not present.

records.segregation: Paternal missense variant carried by clinically unaffected father and brothers; maternal deep intronic variant segregated with disease
quotes: We establish autosomal recessive DES variants p.(Leu190Pro) and a deep intronic splice variant causing inclusion of a frameshift-inducing artificial exon/intronic fragment, as the likely cause of myopathy with cardiac involvement in female siblings.
Both sisters presented in their twenties with slowly progressive limb girdle weakness, severe systolic dysfunction, and progressive, severe respiratory weakness.
Biopsy showed fibre size variation with increased central nuclei. Electron microscopy showed extensive myofibrillar disarray, duplication of the basal lamina, but no inclusions or aggregates.

notes.statement: Riley et al. (2019) showed by RNA sequencing and muscle cDNA studies that a maternal deep intronic DES intron 7 variant caused aberrant splicing of an artificial exon/intronic fragment encoding a premature termination codon, potently activating nonsense-mediated decay (92% paternal DES transcripts, 8% maternal). Western blot showed a 60-75% reduction in desmin, likely comprised only of p.(Leu190Pro) desmin.
quotes: RNA sequencing and studies of muscle cDNA confirmed the deep intronic variant caused aberrant splicing of an artificial exon/intronic fragment into maternal DES mRNA transcripts, encoding a premature termination codon, and potently activating nonsense-mediate decay (92% paternal DES transcripts, 8% maternal).
Western blot showed 60-75% reduction in desmin levels, likely comprised only of missense p.(Leu190Pro) desmin.

notes.statement: Riley et al. (2019) emphasized the continuing importance of muscle biopsy for functional genomic investigation of difficult variants in neuromuscular conditions, noting that the paternal p.(Leu190Pro) variant was initially viewed as unlikely to be causative because heterozygous carriers were unaffected.
quotes: emphasizes the continuing importance of muscle biopsy for functional genomics pursuit of 'tricky' variants in neuromuscular conditions
a paternal missense p.(Leu190Pro) variant was viewed unlikely to be causative of autosomal dominant desminopathy, as the father and brothers carrying this variant were clinically unaffected.

notes.statement: Straub et al. (2018) reported the results of the 229th ENMC international workshop, held in Naarden, the Netherlands, in March 2017, on the nomenclature and reformed classification of the limb-girdle muscular dystrophies.
quotes: 229th ENMC international workshop: Limb girdle muscular dystrophies - Nomenclature and reformed classification Naarden, the Netherlands, 17-19 March 2017.

notes.statement: Ojrzyńska et al. (2017) reported restrictive cardiomyopathy caused by a novel mutation in the desmin gene.
quotes: Restrictive cardiomyopathy due to novel desmin gene mutation.

notes.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) performed genome-wide homozygosity mapping in a consanguineous family with autosomal recessive LGMD and mapped the phenotype to chromosome 2q35-q36.3.
quotes: We performed genome wide homozygosity mapping and mapped the LGMD2 phenotype to chromosome 2q35-q36.3.

notes.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) found that the DES c.1289-2A>G splice site mutation added 16 amino acids within the desmin tail domain; expression and cytoskeletal network formation of mutant desmin were preserved in patient skeletal muscle, but confocal microscopy showed specific disruption of the desmin-lamin B interaction.
quotes: This novel splice site mutation results in addition of 16 amino acids within the tail domain of desmin, which has been suggested to interact with lamin B protein.
Immunofluorescent staining and western blot analysis showed that the expression and the cytoskeletal network formation of mutant desmin were well preserved in skeletal muscle fibres.
We also detected a specific disruption of desmin-lamin B interaction in the skeletal muscle of the patient by confocal laser scanning microscopy.

notes.statement: Cetin et al. (2013) concluded that autosomal recessive DES mutations cause an LGMD2 phenotype without features of myofibrillar myopathy, unlike autosomal dominant desminopathies.
quotes: Our study reveals that autosomal recessive mutations in DES cause LGMD2 phenotype without features of myofibrillar myopathy.

notes.statement: Gudkova et al. (2013) noted that desmin cardiomyopathy can produce a variety of clinical phenotypes, including hypertrophic, restrictive, and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. They described a patient whose disease began in adolescence and changed through several clinical phenotypes over time, which made early diagnosis and treatment difficult.
quotes: However, the disease can result in the variety of clinical phenotypes, including hypertrophic, restrictive, and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
This report describes the first case of desmin cardiomyopathy with early manifestation in adolescence and transformation of several clinical phenotypes over time

notes.statement: Hedberg et al. (2012) noted that earlier studies of this Swedish family had shown linkage to chromosome 10q22.3, but no causative mutation had been found there. Exome sequencing instead identified a mutation in the desmin gene on chromosome 2q35.
quotes: Previous studies had demonstrated linkage to chromosome 10q22.3, but no causative mutation had been found in that region.

notes.statement: Hedberg et al. (2012) concluded that their results showed how useful next-generation sequencing can be. They also highlighted how hard some dominantly inherited muscle diseases are to diagnose, because clinical and morphologic features can vary widely even within one family.
quotes: Our new results demonstrate the usefulness of next-generation sequencing, and the diagnostic difficulties with some forms of dominantly inherited muscle diseases as they can display a wide clinical and morphological variability even within a given family.

notes.statement: Greenberg et al. (2012) used laser capture microdissection to isolate cytoplasmic inclusions from the skeletal muscle of a patient with LGMD1D/1E. Mass spectrometry-based proteomics and bioinformatic analysis of these inclusions identified desmin as their major constituent, which pointed to the causative gene.
quotes: We used laser capture microdissection to isolate cytoplasmic inclusions from skeletal muscle from a patient with LGMD1D/1E, performed mass spectrometry-based proteomics on these minute inclusions, and identified through bioinformatics desmin as their major constituent.

notes.statement: Greenberg et al. (2012) found that the LGMD1D/1E family previously linked to chromosome 6q23 carried a splice donor site mutation in the desmin gene on chromosome 2q35. This finding reassigned the genetic basis of the disorder.
quotes: Sequencing in this patient and family members identified the genetic basis of the previously reported 6q23 linked LGMD1D/1E to be due to an intron splice donor site mutation (IVS3+3A>G) of the desmin gene located on chromosome 2q35.

notes.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) described desmin-related myopathy as an autosomally inherited skeletal and cardiac myopathy, caused mainly by dominant mutations in the desmin gene (DES).
quotes: Desmin-related myopathy (DRM) is an autosomally inherited skeletal and cardiac myopathy, mainly caused by dominant mutations in the desmin gene (DES).

notes.statement: In a meta-analysis of 159 reported carriers of 40 different DES mutations, van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) found neurologic signs in 74% and cardiologic signs in 74% of carriers. Both types of signs occurred in 49%, isolated neurologic signs in 22%, and isolated cardiologic signs in 22%. More than 70% had myopathy or muscle weakness, and one-third of these had normal creatine kinase levels.
quotes: DES mutation carriers (n = 159) with 40 different mutations were included. Neurological signs were present in 74% and cardiological signs in 74% of carriers (both neurological and cardiological signs in 49%, isolated neurological signs in 22%, and isolated cardiological signs in 22%).
More than 70% of carriers exhibited myopathy or muscular weakness, with normal creatine kinase levels present in one third of them.

notes.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) found that up to 50% of DES mutation carriers had cardiomyopathy and about 60% had cardiac conduction disease or arrhythmias, with atrioventricular block as an important hallmark. Symptoms generally began in the thirties, and a quarter of carriers died at a mean age of 49 years. Two patients with pacemakers died suddenly, suggesting ventricular tachyarrhythmia as the cause of death.
quotes: Up to 50% of carriers had cardiomyopathy and around 60% had cardiac conduction disease or arrhythmias, with atrioventricular block as an important hallmark.
Symptoms generally started during the 30s; a quarter of carriers died at a mean age of 49 years.
Sudden cardiac death occurred in two patients with a pacemaker, suggesting a ventricular tachyarrhythmia as cause of death.

notes.statement: van Spaendonck-Zwarts et al. (2011) found that most DES mutations were missense mutations, mostly located in the 2B domain. Mutations in the 2B domain predominated in patients with an isolated neurologic phenotype, whereas mutations in the head and tail domains predominated in patients with an isolated cardiologic phenotype.
quotes: The majority of DES mutations were missense mutations, mostly located in the 2B domain.

Mutations in the 2B domain were predominant in patients with an isolated neurological phenotype, whereas head and tail domain mutations were predominant in patients with an isolated cardiological phenotype.

notes.statement: Otten et al. (2010) found by immunohistochemistry of myocardial tissue from 2 p.R454W DES mutation carriers that, besides desmin aggregates, there was less desmoplakin and plakophilin-2 at the intercalated disk. They suggested a link between desmosomal cardiomyopathies and cardiomyopathies caused by DES mutations.
quotes: In addition to desmin aggregates, immunohistochemistry demonstrated a decreased amount of desmoplakin and plakophilin-2 at the intercalated disk in p.R454W mutation carriers.
suggesting a link between desmosomal cardiomyopathies (mainly affecting the right ventricle) and cardiomyopathies caused by DES mutations

notes.statement: Otten et al. (2010) screened the DES gene in 50 patients with ARVC or an ARVC-like phenotype and found no further DES mutations. They concluded that an ARVC-like phenotype or severe cardiomyopathy with right ventricular involvement is a possible but infrequent cardiac phenotype in desmin-related myopathy.
quotes: The DES gene was screened for mutations in 50 ARVC(-like) patients.
we did not find additional DES mutations in ARVC(-like) patients
We confirmed that either an ARVC-like phenotype or a severe cardiomyopathy with right ventricular involvement are possible, yet infrequent, cardiac phenotypes in DRM.

notes.statement: In cardiac tissue from DES p.S13F carriers, van Tintelen et al. (2009) found normal amounts of the major desmosomal proteins. However, the intercalated disks were more convoluted and elongated and had a zigzag appearance. The authors suggested that a localized effect of desmin on intercalated disk structure might contribute to disease pathogenesis.
quotes: Normal amounts of the major desmosomal proteins were found, but the intercalated disks were more convoluted and elongated and had a zigzag appearance.
A localized effect of desmin on the structure of the cardiac intercalated disks might contribute to disease pathogenesis.

notes.statement: van Tintelen et al. (2009) identified the DES p.S13F head domain mutation as a founder mutation shared by 5 families.
quotes: All 27 carriers or obligate carriers of a p.S13F DES founder mutation demonstrated a fully penetrant yet variable phenotype.

notes.statement: van Tintelen et al. (2009) described the phenotype of the DES p.S13F mutation as variable but mainly cardiac. Features included conduction disease at an early age and right ventricular involvement, including right bundle branch block, right ventricular tachycardias, and phenocopies of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
quotes: patients show a variable yet predominantly cardiologic phenotype characterized by conduction disease at an early age and RV involvement including right bundle branch block and/or RV tachycardias and arrhythmogenic RV cardiomyopathy phenocopies

notes.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) considered their patient the first case of infantile-onset desmin-associated cardiomyopathy and the first case exhaustively proven to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait; the heterozygous parents were unaffected.
quotes: Our observation is the first known case of infantile-onset desmin mutation-associated cardiomyopathy and the first case exhaustively proven to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
did not cause pathogenic effects in the patient’s parents who are heterozygous for the p.Arg173_Glu179del alteration.

notes.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) noted that the homozygous p.Arg173_Glu179del mutation, which removes a full heptad at the start of the 1B domain, prevented assembly of desmin filaments and compromised intermediate filament network formation in transiently transfected MCF-7 cells.
quotes: The homozygous p.Arg173_Glu179del mutation prevented assembly of desmin filaments and compromised the ability of desmin to form an intermediate filament network in transiently transfected MCF-7 cells, providing a confirmation of high pathogenic potential.
The mutation abolishes part of protein structure representing a full heptad.

notes.statement: Piñol-Ripoll et al. (2009) concluded that patients with desmin-related cardiomyopathy are at high risk of ventricular arrhythmia and should be considered candidates for implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement even before ventricular dysfunction becomes evident.
quotes: The current observation additionally confirms that patients with desmin-related cardiomyopathy are at high risk of developing ventricular arrhythmia and therefore should be considered candidates for AICD implantation even before ventricular dysfunction becomes evident.

notes.statement: Kuhl et al. (2008) re-examined the Swedish family with autosomal dominant MFM and ARVC7 using a high-density SNP array and confirmed linkage to 10q22.3, with no other regions showing significant linkage. They narrowed the critical interval to 4.27 Mbp between D10S1645 and D10S1786, containing 18 candidate genes, 17 of which are shared with the CMD1C region.
quotes: re-examined and confirmed the previous linkage data for ARVC7 using a high-density single nucleotide polymorphism marker panel from Affymetrix (Human Mapping 10K Array). No other regions with significant evidence for linkage were discovered.
The critical interval was narrowed down to 4.27 Mbp between D10S1645 and D10S1786. This reduced the total number of candidate genes to 18 of which 17

notes.statement: Kuhl et al. (2008) found no disease-causing mutation in the coding regions of the candidate genes in the linked region, and excluded VCL and LDB3 by sequencing. Using hybrid cell lines carrying only the affected or normal chromosome 10 homolog, they found no submicroscopic or intragenic deletions, and speculated that regulatory mutations in one of the 18 genes are responsible.
quotes: No disease-causing mutation was found in their coding regions. Moreover, metavinculin (VCL) and ZASP/cypher (LDB3) proximal and distal to this linked region were excluded by sequence analysis.
All sequence tagged sites and exons were present on both homologs. We speculate that regulatory mutations in 1 of the 18 genes from 10q22.3 are responsible

notes.statement: Pica et al. (2008) noted that the S13F mutation lay at a protein kinase C phosphorylation site within a highly conserved nonapeptide sequence in the head domain of desmin.
quotes: The mutation is located at a protein kinase-C phosphorylation site within a highly conserved nonapeptide sequence in the head domain of the desmin protein.

notes.statement: Pica et al. (2008) found that expressing the S13F mutant desmin cDNA in cell lines caused large desmin accumulations, while a filamentous network was still preserved.
quotes: Expression of the mutant desmin cDNA in cell lines induced large desmin accumulations associated with preservation of a filamentous network.

notes.statement: Bergman et al. (2007) found intracytoplasmic desmin aggregates, staining for desmin and p62, in muscle biopsies from patients with the DES S13F mutation.
quotes: Morphological analysis of muscle biopsies revealed intracytoplasmic desmin aggregates (desmin and p62 staining).

notes.statement: Bergman et al. (2007) stressed that the desmin gene should be analyzed in patients with (familial) cardiac conduction disease, dilated cardiomyopathy, and/or a progressive skeletal myopathy resembling limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
quotes: This article illustrates the importance of analysing the desmin gene in patients with (familial) cardiac conduction disease, dilated cardiomyopathy and/or a progressive skeletal myopathy resembling limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

notes.statement: Bär et al. (2007) reported 3 novel mutations in the non-alpha-helical carboxy-terminal tail domain of desmin (DES) in patients with myopathies: T442I, R454W, and S460I.
quotes: Here we report three novel mutations--c.1325C>T (p.T442I), c.1360C>T (p.R454W), and c.1379G>T (p.S460I)--located in desmin's non-alpha-helical carboxy-terminal "tail" domain.

notes.statement: Bär et al. (2007) studied 7 desmin tail mutations (the 3 novel ones plus E413K, K449T, I451M, and V469M). Two mutants (E413K and R454W) failed to assemble into intermediate filaments in vitro. All except E413K were incorporated into filament arrays in transfected C2C12 cells. Filament properties still differed significantly from wildtype in viscometric assembly assays.
quotes: Although all but two mutants (p.E413K, p.R454W) assembled into IFs in vitro and all except p.E413K were incorporated into IF arrays in transfected C2C12 cells, filament properties differed significantly from wild-type desmin as revealed by viscometric assembly assays.

notes.statement: Bär et al. (2007) found that the desmin tail mutants, when coassembled with wildtype desmin, severely disturbed filament formation and filament-filament interactions. This indicated an inherent incompatibility between mutant and wildtype protein in forming mixed filaments. The authors suggested that the various clinical phenotypes may reflect altered interactions of the tail domain with different cytoskeletal components.
quotes: Most notably, when coassembled with wild-type desmin, these mutants revealed a severe disturbance of filament-formation competence and filament-filament interactions, indicating an inherent incompatibility of mutant and wild-type protein to form mixed filaments.
The various clinical phenotypes observed may reflect altered interactions of desmin's tail domain with different components of the myoblast cytoskeleton

notes.statement: Bär et al. (2007) proposed their in vitro assembly regimen as a sensitive tool for detecting whether a particular desmin mutation can cause filament abnormalities.
quotes: Our in vitro assembly regimen proved to be a very sensible tool to detect if a particular desmin mutation is able to cause filament abnormalities.

notes.statement: Shelton et al. (2004) reported a 1-year-old male Australian Shepherd dog with chronic lameness, contractures, exercise intolerance, elevated serum creatine kinase, complex repetitive discharges on electromyography, and clinically identified cardiomyopathy. Light and electron microscopy and immunohistochemistry of muscle biopsies showed a myofibrillar myopathy with accumulation of desmin and other proteins. The authors stated that this was the first report of myofibrillar myopathy in the dog.
quotes: A 1-year-old male neutered Australian Shepherd dog was referred to a veterinary specialist for evaluation of chronic lameness, contractures, and exercise intolerance. Serum creatine kinase was elevated, and electromyography showed complex repetitive discharges. Cardiomyopathy was clinically identified.

Muscle biopsies evaluated by light and electron microscopy, and immunohistochemistry revealed the presence of a myofibrillar myopathy with accumulation of desmin and other proteins. These observations represent the first report of myofibrillar myopathy in the dog.

notes.statement: Ferreiro et al. (2004) noted that mutations in the desmin and alpha-B crystallin genes account for about one-third of desmin-related myopathy cases. In the original German family with early-onset, recessive desmin-related myopathy with Mallory body-like inclusions, they found linkage to the SEPN1 locus on 1p36 and a homozygous 92-nucleotide SEPN1 deletion. This showed that desmin-related myopathy is molecularly heterogeneous.
quotes: Mutations in the desmin and the alpha-B crystallin genes account for approximately one third of the DRM cases.

In the original MB-DRM German family, we demonstrated a linkage of the disease to the SEPN1 locus (1p36), and subsequently a homozygous SEPN1 deletion (del 92 nucleotide -19/+73) in the affected patients.
These findings substantiate the molecular heterogeneity of DRM

notes.statement: Selcen et al. (2004) screened 63 unrelated patients with myofibrillar myopathy (MFM) for mutations in four genes: desmin, alphaB-crystallin, telethonin and syncoilin. Four patients had missense mutations in the head or tail region of desmin. Two had truncating mutations in the C-terminal domain of alphaB-crystallin. None had a mutation in syncoilin or telethonin. The authors concluded that MFM is morphologically distinct but genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: Two of the 63 patients carry truncation mutations in the C-terminal domain of alphaBC, four carry missense mutations in the head or tail region of desmin, and none carries a mutation in syncoilin or telethonin.
Thus, MFM is morphologically distinct but genetically heterogeneous.

notes.statement: In the 63 patients with myofibrillar myopathy studied by Selcen et al. (2004), mean age at onset was 54 +/- 16 years. Weakness was both proximal and distal in 77% of patients and proximal only in 13%. Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 16%. Electromyography showed a myopathic pattern with abnormal electrical irritability.
quotes: The age of onset was 54 +/- 16 years (mean +/- SD). Weakness was both proximal and distal in 77% and proximal only in 13%. Cardiomyopathy was diagnosed in 16%.
Electro myography revealed a myopathic pattern associated with abnormal electrical irritability

notes.statement: Selcen et al. (2004) found that, on average, 90% of abnormal muscle fibers in myofibrillar myopathy abnormally expressed myotilin, compared with 75% for desmin and alphaB-crystallin and 70% for dystrophin and beta-amyloid precursor protein. They concluded that immunostains for these proteins, especially myotilin, are useful adjuncts in diagnosis. Abnormal fibers were best identified in trichrome-stained sections by their congophilic hyaline structures.
quotes: among the abnormal fibres, an average of 90, 75, 75, 70 and 70% abnormally express myotilin, desmin, alphaBC, dystrophin and beta-amyloid precursor protein, respectively. Therefore, immunostains for these proteins, and especially for myotilin, are useful adjuncts in the diagnosis of MFM.
The hyaline structures are strongly congophilic.

notes.statement: On electron microscopy, Selcen et al. (2004) observed progressive myofibrillar degeneration starting at the Z-disk in myofibrillar myopathy. They also found accumulation of degraded filamentous material and dislocated membranous organelles trapped in autophagic vacuoles.
quotes: Electron microscopy shows progressive myofibrillar degeneration commencing at the Z-disk, accumulation of degraded filamentous material and entrapment of dislocated membranous organelles in autophagic vacuoles.

notes.statement: Kaminska et al. (2004) found by structural analysis that the desmin E359_S361 deletion introduced a second stutter immediately downstream of the naturally occurring stutter in the 2B coiled-coil segment, doubling the extent of local coiled-coil unwinding, whereas the N366del mutation converted the wildtype stutter into a stammer, expected to cause extra overwinding of the coiled-coil.
quotes: Structural analysis reveals that the E359_S361 deletion introduces a second stutter immediately downstream of the naturally occurring stutter, thus doubling the extent of the local coiled-coil unwinding.

The N366del mutation converts the wild-type stutter into a different type of discontinuity, a stammer. A stammer, as opposed to a stutter, is expected to cause an extra overwinding of the coiled-coil.

notes.statement: Kaminska et al. (2004) showed by expression studies in two cell lines that desmin molecules carrying these in-frame deletions were unable to polymerize into a functional filamentous network, consistent with fatal damage to desmin filament assembly.
quotes: These mutations alter the coiled-coil geometry in specific ways leading to fatal damage to desmin filament assembly.
Expression studies in two cell lines confirm the inability of desmin molecules with this changed architecture to polymerize into a functional filamentous network.

notes.statement: Park et al. (2000) showed by expression of genomic DNA fragments that the DES IVS3+3A-G and IVS2-1G-A mutations caused skipping of exon 3, resulting in an in-frame deletion of 32 codons predicted to remove 32 amino acids from the 1B segment of the alpha-helical rod.
quotes: Expression of genomic DNA fragments carrying the IVS3+3A-->G and IVS2-1G-->A mutations confirmed that these mutations cause exon 3 deletion.
Aberrant splicing leads to an in frame deletion of 32 complete codons and is predicted to result in mutant desmin lacking 32 amino acids from the 1B segment of the alpha helical rod.

notes.statement: Park et al. (2000) found that expression of the exon 3-deleted mutant desmin in vimentin-deficient SW13 cells resulted in aggregation of abnormal coarse clumps of desmin-positive material throughout the cytoplasm.
quotes: Functional analysis of the mutant desmin in SW13 (vim-) cells showed aggregation of abnormal coarse clumps of desmin positive material dispersed throughout the cytoplasm.

notes.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) found a maximum 2-point lod score of 2.76 at marker D10S1752 and a multipoint peak lod score of 3.06 between D10S605 and D10S215 in a Swedish family with myofibrillar myopathy and ARVC. These results suggested linkage to chromosome 10q22.3.
quotes: Linkage analysis of candidate chromosomal regions showed a maximum 2-point LOD score of 2.76 for marker locus D10S1752 on chromosome 10q.
A multipoint peak LOD score of 3.06 between markers D10S605 and D10S215 suggests linkage to chromosome 10q22.3

notes.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) concluded that the disorder in the Swedish family was inherited in an autosomal dominant manner, with variable onset and severity of skeletal muscle and cardiac involvement.
quotes: Inheritance is autosomal dominant with variable onset and severity of skeletal muscle and cardiac involvement.

notes.statement: Melberg et al. (1999) found that weakness was axial in mildly affected patients, axial and mainly distal in moderately affected patients, and generalized in severely affected patients. Muscle biopsies showed rimmed vacuoles and accumulation of desmin, dystrophin and other proteins, and electron microscopy showed granulofilamentous changes.
quotes: The distribution of weakness was axial in mildly affected, axial and predominantly distal in moderately affected, and generalized in severely affected patients.
Muscle biopsy specimens showed myopathic changes, rimmed vacuoles, and accumulation of desmin, dystrophin, and other proteins.

notes.statement: By linkage analysis in a large family with autosomal dominant distal myopathy with desmin accumulation and cardiomyopathy, Saavedra-Matiz et al. (2000) mapped the disease gene to chromosome 2q33, within a 17-cM segment bounded by markers D2S2248 and D2S401. They considered desmin the best candidate gene.
quotes: have mapped the location of the gene causing the myopathy to human chromosome 2q33. The gene is within a 17-cM segment of chromosome 2q bounded by the DNA markers D2S2248 and D2S401. The best candidate gene for this myopathy is desmin.

notes.statement: Sjöberg et al. (1999) found that the L345P desmin missense mutation lay at an evolutionarily highly conserved position of the coiled-coil rod domain important for dimer formation.
quotes: The mutation is located in an evolutionarily highly conserved position of the desmin coiled-coil rod domain important for dimer formation.

notes.statement: Sjöberg et al. (1999) showed that L345P desmin could not form filamentous networks in transfected HeLa and SW13 cells. They concluded that the mutation causes myopathy by interfering in a dominant-negative manner with the dimerization-polymerization process of intermediate filament assembly.
quotes: L345P desmin is incapable of forming filamentous networks in transfected HeLa and SW13 cells.
We conclude that the L345P desmin missense mutation causes myopathy by interfering in a dominant-negative manner with the dimerization-polymerization process of intermediate filament assembly.

notes.statement: Muñoz-Mármol et al. (1998) found that recombinant desmin carrying the 7-amino acid coiled-coil deletion could not form proper desmin intermediate filament networks in cultured cells and could not assemble into 10-nm filaments in vitro. The authors concluded that this was direct evidence that a desmin mutation can cause human myopathies.
quotes: We show that recombinant desmin harboring this deletion cannot form proper desmin intermediate filament networks in cultured cells, nor is it able to assemble into 10-nm filaments in vitro.
These findings provide direct evidence that a mutation in desmin can cause human myopathies.

notes.statement: Muñoz-Mármol et al. (1998) found no wild-type desmin allele in muscle tissue from their patient.
quotes: Muscle tissue from this patient lacks the wild-type desmin allele

notes.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) described desmin-related myopathy as a familial disorder with skeletal muscle weakness associated with cardiac conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and restrictive heart failure, and with intracytoplasmic accumulation of desmin-reactive deposits in cardiac and skeletal muscle cells.
quotes: Desmin-related myopathy (OMIM 601419) is a familial disorder characterized by skeletal muscle weakness associated with cardiac conduction blocks, arrhythmias and restrictive heart failure, and by intracytoplasmic accumulation of desmin-reactive deposits in cardiac and skeletal muscle cells.

notes.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) found that the mutations in the 2 families lay in the highly conserved carboxy-terminal end of the desmin rod domain.
quotes: We report two new families with desmin-related cardioskeletal myopathy associated with mutations in the highly conserved carboxy-terminal end of the desmin rod domain.

notes.statement: Goldfarb et al. (1998) noted that involvement of the DES gene had been excluded in 3 families diagnosed with desmin-related myopathy.
quotes: Involvement of the desmin gene (DES) has been excluded in three families diagnosed with desmin-related myopathy.

notes.statement: In a review of distal myopathies, Barohn et al. (1998) identified 5 distinct predominantly distal myopathies with discrete clinical and genetic patterns: Welander, Markesbery-Griggs/Udd, Nonaka, Miyoshi, and Laing myopathies. They noted that disorders allelic to the distal myopathies can begin with proximal weakness.
quotes: Five distinct predominantly distal myopathies have been identified with discrete clinical and genetic patterns as follows
However, it is already clear that disorders allelic to the distal myopathies can begin with proximal weakness.

notes.statement: In a family with autosomal dominant dilated cardiomyopathy, conduction-system disease and adult-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (FDC-CDM), Messina et al. (1997) ran a genomewide scan. They found linkage of the myopathy to chromosome 6q (maximum lod score of 4.99 at theta = 0.00 for D6S262). Haplotype analysis narrowed the region to a 3-cM interval between D6S1705 and D6S1656.
quotes: A genomewide scan identified a region on the long arm of chromosome 6 that is significantly associated with the presence of myopathy (D6S262; maximum LOD score [Z(max)] 4.99 at maximum recombination fraction [theta(max)] .00), identifying FDC-CDM as a genetically distinct disease.
Haplotype analysis refined the interval containing the genetic defect, to a 3-cM interval between D6S1705 and D6S1656.

notes.statement: Using linkage analysis, Messina et al. (1997) excluded the genomic regions already known to be linked to dilated cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy phenotypes in this family. They concluded that these disorders are genetically heterogeneous.
quotes: Genetic linkage was used to exclude regions of the genome known to be linked to dilated cardiomyopathy and muscular dystrophy phenotypes and to confirm genetic heterogeneity of these disorders.

notes.statement: In the FDC-CDM family, Messina et al. (1997) used haplotype analysis to exclude several striated muscle-expressed candidate genes in the 6q region: laminin alpha-2, laminin alpha-4, triadin and phospholamban.
quotes: This haplotype analysis excludes a number of striated muscle-expressed genes present in this region, including laminin alpha2, laminin alpha4, triadin, and phospholamban.

notes.statement: Vajsar et al. (1993) found that follow-up muscle biopsies 6 years later showed more fibers containing subsarcolemmal aggregates that stained positively for desmin and ubiquitin. This indicated that the pathology progressed over time.
quotes: Follow up muscle biopsies six years later showed an increased number of the muscle fibres that contained subsarcolemmal aggregates that stained positively for desmin and ubiquitin.

notes.statement: Vajsar et al. (1993) concluded that these clinical and pathologic features characterized a rare familial myopathy. They associated it with an unusual distribution of desmin intermediate filament proteins in skeletal muscle and probably also in cardiac muscle.
quotes: These clinical and pathological features characterise a rare familial myopathy associated with an unusual distribution of desmin intermediate filament proteins in skeletal and probably also cardiac muscle.

notes.statement: Abe et al. (1993) found that affected members of a Japanese kindred became disabled 5 to 10 years after onset because of chronic respiratory failure. Males were affected more often than females, in a ratio of 2:1.
quotes: the patients became disabled after 5 to 10 years due to chronic respiratory failure
Males were more frequently affected than females (2:1).

notes.statement: Horowitz and Schmalbruch (1994) found that muscle biopsies from multiple members of the family, taken at different stages of disease, showed desmin storage and autophagocytosis. On electromyography there was prominent spontaneous activity, short-duration motor unit potentials, and polyphasia.
quotes: Muscle biopsies from multiple family members at different stages of the disease are characterized by desmin storage and autophagocytosis.
On electromyography there is prominent spontaneous activity, short duration motor unit potentials, and polyphasia.

notes.statement: Horowitz and Schmalbruch (1994) concluded that this distal myopathy differed from other phenotypically similar distal myopathies in its rapid progression, fatal course, and pathologic features. They stated that the role and specificity of excessive desmin accumulation in this and other myopathic and cardiac disorders were unknown.
quotes: This distal myopathy differs from other phenotypically similar disorders in its rapidity of progression, fatal course and pathologic features.
The role and specificity of excessive desmin accumulation in this and other myopathic and cardiac disorders are unknown.

notes.statement: Ariza et al. (1995) concluded that desmin myopathy is a multisystem disorder and reported intestinal smooth muscle involvement for the first time, in addition to its known skeletal and cardiac muscle manifestations. They considered the coexisting neurofilament aggregates in the spinal cord and roots an extremely rare combination of intermediate filament pathology in the neuromuscular system.
quotes: These widely distributed findings illustrate the multisystemic character of desmin myopathy, which in this instance first adds intestinal smooth muscle involvement to its already known skeletal and cardiac muscle manifestations.
The additional presence of neurofilament aggregates in the spinal cord and roots constitutes an extremely rare conjunction of intermediate filament pathology of the neuromuscular system.

notes.statement: Goebel (1995) reviewed desmin-related neuromuscular disorders and noted that desmin pathology was always marked by increased amounts of desmin, either diffusely or focally. Focal desmin accretion occurred in conjunction with cytoplasmic and spheroid bodies or as patchy granulofilamentous material, and both lesions had been found in certain families affected by myopathy and/or cardiomyopathy.
quotes: The pathology of desmin in human neuromuscular disorders is always marked by increased amounts, diffusely or focally.

Focal accretion of desmin may be twofold, in conjunction with certain inclusion bodies, cytoplasmic and spheroid bodies, and in a more patchy fashion, granulofilamentous material. Both lesions have been found in certain families, affected by a myopathy and/or cardiomyopathy.

notes.statement: Goebel (1995) noted that other proteins, such as dystrophin, vimentin, actin, ubiquitin, and alpha-B crystallin, may also be overexpressed, and suggested that desmin pathology may be genetically regulated or may merely reflect profoundly impaired metabolism of several proteins within myofibers.
quotes: Other proteins, e.g., dystrophin, vimentin, actin, ubiquitin, and alpha-B crystallin, may also be overexpressed. Desmin pathology may be genetically regulated or may merely reflect profoundly impaired metabolism of several proteins within myofibers.

notes.statement: Porte et al. (1980) suggested that a disturbance in the metabolism of desmin, the protein subunit of intermediate filaments and a fundamental component of Z bands, might be involved in this type of cardiomyopathy; they also proposed a possible role for a chronic defect in calcium regulation given the marked sarcoplasmic reticulum abnormalities.
quotes: These observations suggest that disturbance in the metabolism of desmin (protein subunit of intermediate filaments and a fundamental component of Z bands) might be involved in this type of cardiomyopathy.
The influence of a chronic defect in calcium regulation might also be envisaged in view of the marked SR abnormalities.

notes.statement: Wolburg et al. (1982) considered that the disorder was caused by a basic defect of myofilament biosynthesis. They suggested this defect was presumably evoked by a neurogenic factor affecting the trophic influence of the neuron on the muscle cell.
quotes: A basic defect of myofilament biosynthesis is considered to be the cause of the disorder. It is presumably evoked by a neurogenic factor affecting the trophic influence of the neuron on the muscle cell.

notes.statement: Wolburg et al. (1982) found that the skeletal muscle inclusions consisted of dense granular and fine filamentous components consistent with cytoplasmic bodies. They noted that cytoplasmic bodies are a nonspecific type of inclusion but were the outstanding structural anomaly in both patients.
quotes: Inclusions consisting of dense granular and fine filamentous components were found in skeletal muscle fibers
Although cytoplasmic bodies are a nonspecific type of inclusion, they were the outstanding structural anomaly in both cases.

notes.statement: Chapon et al. (1989) noted that cytoplasmic body myopathy with familial incidence has rarely been reported. It has been even more rarely revealed by respiratory insufficiency in adult life.
quotes: Familial cytoplasmic body myopathy with familial incidence has rarely been reported and still more rarely has been revealed by respiratory insufficiency in adult life.
